messages.message:

Gunakan konfigurasi yang tersedia saat ini. Bandingkan durasi sebelum pembulatan; bulatkan hasil durasi dua desimal dengan nilai tengah menjauh dari nol. Untuk T1 gunakan seluruh tipe detail tidak null; evaluasi SPM/SLA menggunakan detail type=booth per gardu. LHR dibulatkan ke integer terdekat dengan nilai tengah menjauh dari nol. Urutkan array: golongan berdasarkan ID; bulan kronologis; insiden berdasarkan tanggal lalu ID; penyebab/aset berdasarkan jumlah menurun lalu ID; evaluasi berdasarkan nomor gardu lalu kode; kegagalan berdasarkan tanggal, ID monitoring, nomor gardu, kode; indikator berdasarkan kode.

---
name: "hka-trom-business-context"
description: "Interpret HKA TROM operational data and analytical requests involving transaction monitoring, traffic volume and LHR, incidents and accident causes, inspection damage, or transaction SPM/SLA compliance."
---

# HKA TROM Business Context

HKA TROM is HK Aston's operational information system for managed toll roads. Its records describe monitoring observations, traffic counts, incident handling, and asset inspections. This package supplies the institutional meanings needed to analyze those records.

## Shared context

A **section (ruas)** contains **gates (gerbang)**; a gate contains **booths (gardu)**. Reports and observations have different grains: a monitoring report, a booth sample, a traffic count, an incident, and an inspection item are different units of analysis.

Use the requested section, gate, and operational date scope. Record creation and update timestamps describe administration, not when the operational event occurred. Explicit date ranges include both endpoints. A named calendar month means that month's full calendar span; a month-to-date request has a different endpoint.

This package defines business semantics. The connected data catalogue defines available entities, fields, relationships, and access scope. Master data supplies current identities and labels; effective configuration supplies section-specific SPM/SLA parameters. Resolve names against those records and use their IDs to preserve identity. A requested output contract defines answer fields, labels, and display precision; it does not change the underlying business quantity. If necessary scope, configuration, or a business definition is unavailable or contradictory, state the gap rather than silently substituting a value.

## Domain references

Read the reference for each domain involved in the request. For a request spanning domains, use each relevant reference.

| Request concerns | Read | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| Indonesian terms, organizational scope, or record identity | [Terminology](references/terminology.md) | Shared vocabulary, master entities, dates and identifiers |
| Transaction duration, monitoring reports, or booth samples | [Transactions](references/transactions.md) | Observation grain, sample meanings, overall average |
| Vehicle volume, vehicle classes, LHR, or monthly traffic trends | [Traffic](references/traffic.md) | Counts, calendar denominator, zero-volume classes |
| Incident status, unresolved incidents, accidents, or causes | [Incidents](references/incidents.md) | Handling state and cause assignments |
| Inspection condition, damage categories, repair priorities, or asset summaries | [Inspections](references/inspections.md) | Item hierarchy, damage population, asset attribution |
| Transaction-speed SPM/SLA, failures, period status, or period comparison | [Transaction SPM/SLA](references/spm-sla.md) and [Transactions](references/transactions.md) | Evaluation grain, rule family, applicability and compliance meanings |

These references cover the listed operational domains. Other TROM modules or SPM families require their own business definitions.

===== spm-sla.md =====
# Transaction SPM/SLA

## Indicator family

These rules concern average transaction duration per monitored booth. They do not define queue-length, incident-response, equipment, or other SPM families.

| Rule code | Indicator label |
|---|---|
| `kecepatan-transaksi-1` | Gerbang tol sistem terbuka |
| `kecepatan-transaksi-2` | Gerbang tol sistem tertutup (Gardu Masuk) |
| `kecepatan-transaksi-3` | Gerbang tol sistem tertutup (Gardu Keluar) |
| `kecepatan-transaksi-4` | GTO (Gardu Tol Ambil Kartu) |
| `kecepatan-transaksi-5` | Gardu Tol Transaksi |

Each monitored booth average is evaluated against **all five indicators** configured for its section. The indicator labels do not select one exclusive rule based on an inferred gate type.

## Governed configuration

`effective_spm_sla_config` supplies each section's rule identity, descriptions, comparison operator, SPM threshold, SLA threshold, SLA applicability, and unit. Thresholds and applicability belong to that effective configuration, not to a universal table of constants in this package.

SPM and SLA are separate targets for the same measurement. SLA applicability is per section and indicator: all, some, or none of a section's indicators can have an applicable SLA. A numeric SLA parameter alone does not establish applicability. Missing configuration is not the same as explicitly non-applicable SLA.

When a section has no SLA override for an active indicator, the effective configuration uses the SPM parameter and specification as the SLA defaults and marks SLA applicable. An explicit section override controls its own threshold and applicability. These defaults are already resolved in `effective_spm_sla_config`; an absent effective rule or an applicable rule without a threshold remains a configuration gap.

## Measurement and evaluation grain

The measurement is the arithmetic mean of `transaction_duration` samples with `type = booth`, for **one booth within one monitoring report**. It is measured in seconds. Other observation types, including `longbooth`, are outside this transaction-speed compliance population.

A booth's samples have equal weight within that mean. The same booth number in another report is a separate measurement. Valid booth numbers run from 1 through the report's declared `total_booth`. Out-of-range booth numbers or null-duration booth samples are data-quality gaps, not evidence of zero duration. A declared booth with no samples has no observed average; declared booth counts are not sample counts.

One evaluation is identified by monitoring-report ID, booth number, and indicator identity. Its operational date, section, gate, and shift belong to the monitoring report. The same measurement can pass one indicator and fail another because the thresholds differ.

## Compliance states

A measurement passes a target when it satisfies the configured operator and threshold in the configured unit. For this transaction-speed family, the current operator is `<=` and the unit is seconds: equality passes. Compliance uses the unrounded booth average; display rounding must not change the decision.

An applicable SLA has its own pass/fail result. A non-applicable SLA has no pass/fail result: its event result is null and its summary state is `not_applicable`. SPM remains evaluable when SLA is non-applicable.

A failure detail describes an evaluation where SPM failed, applicable SLA failed, or both. Both failures can belong to the same evaluation.

## Period meaning

For an indicator over a period containing evaluations, period status is **fail if any evaluation fails, otherwise pass**. This applies independently to SPM and applicable SLA. A period-wide average does not replace the individual booth evaluations.

Evaluation count measures booth/report/indicator evaluations, not source samples. Failed count measures the subset that failed the corresponding target. Non-applicable SLA has zero applicable evaluations, zero failures, and state `not_applicable`.

A period with no observations provides no measured compliance evidence. This package does not assign a no-observation compliance default; report that gap rather than presenting it as an observed pass.

A period comparison retains each period's status, evaluation count, and failed count for the same section and indicator. A change between pass and fail is a compliance change; a change involving `not_applicable` is an applicability change. Different observation counts describe different coverage, even if the status is unchanged.

===== transactions.md =====
# Transaction Monitoring

## Records and grain

| Entity | Meaning and relationship |
|---|---|
| `monitoring_transactions` | One monitoring report with section, gate, operational `date`, shift schedule, and declared booth counts. |
| `monitoring_transaction_details` | One recorded sample belonging to its parent report through `transaction_id`. `type` identifies the observation kind and `booth_number` identifies the booth within the report. |

`transaction_duration` measures elapsed transaction time in **seconds**. The label “transaction speed” refers to this duration; a smaller value means a faster transaction. `vehicle_queue` is a separate queue observation and is not a duration or a traffic-volume total.

`total_booth` describes the report's declared booths. It is not the number of samples. A report can contain several observations of the same booth, and different booths or reports can contain different sample counts.

## Overall average duration

The overall average transaction duration is the arithmetic mean of the matching non-null detail-level duration observations under the requested parent-report scope. Each observed duration has equal weight. Null duration contributes neither a value nor an observation to this mean. The standard summary includes matching detail types; it has no implicit `type = booth` restriction.

This quantity differs from an equally weighted mean of report averages or booth averages when sample counts differ. A request explicitly asking for those other grains has a different meaning.

The standard duration summary is reported to two decimal places. It uses `0.00` when there are no duration observations; this is an empty-summary convention, not evidence of instantaneous service.

## Booth compliance

Transaction-speed compliance uses a separate population and grain defined in [Transaction SPM/SLA](spm-sla.md). An overall section average does not establish whether each monitored booth met its service targets.

===== terminology.md =====
# Terminology and Scope

## Operational vocabulary

| Term | Meaning in this package |
|---|---|
| Ruas / section | Managed toll-road section; the organizational scope for reports and section-specific service targets. |
| Gerbang / gate | Toll gate belonging to a section. |
| Gardu / booth | A numbered toll booth observed within a transaction-monitoring report. A booth number alone is not a global identifier. |
| Shift | Operational shift associated with a monitoring report through a dated, section-specific shift schedule. |
| Monitoring transaksi | A report containing sampled transaction-duration and queue observations; it is not a ledger of every paid toll transaction. |
| Golongan kendaraan / vehicle class | Configured vehicle classification used to group traffic counts. |
| LHR / Lalu Lintas Harian Rata-rata | Average daily traffic volume over a calendar period; its denominator is defined in [Traffic](traffic.md). |
| Insiden / incident | Recorded operational event with zero or more handling actions. An accident is an incident identified by the accident flag. |
| Tindakan penanganan / handling action | An incident response action carrying its own progress stage. |
| Inspeksi / inspection | Inspection event containing elements and their recorded inspection items. |
| Aset / asset | Inspection/maintenance asset-master entry identified through the inspection's scheduled asset assignment; see [Inspections](inspections.md) for its grain. |
| SPM / Standar Pelayanan Minimal | Minimum service standard represented by configured indicators. |
| SLA / Service Level Agreement | Section-specific service target whose applicability is configured per indicator. |

## Master identities

`toll_sections` and `toll_gates` identify the managed scope. `shift_schedules` identifies monitoring shifts; `vehicle_classes` identifies traffic classifications. Names, short names, and codes are labels for their master IDs, not independent entities. Current master records determine the available sections, gates, shifts, and classes.

A shift number can recur on different dates and in different sections. The schedule ID identifies that dated assignment; the shift number alone does not identify a monitoring event.

Entity names in this package refer to the governed data catalogue. Available fields and their exact spellings come from that catalogue; production storage names can differ.

## Dates and relationships

Operational date belongs to the parent event: monitoring report, traffic report, incident, or inspection. Child records inherit that event's scope through their documented relationship. In production TROM, the incident's operational date is named `accident_date`, including for incidents that are not accidents.

A field named `transaction_id` is local to its domain: monitoring details belong to a monitoring report, while traffic-volume details belong to a traffic report. Equal numeric IDs across these domains do not establish a relationship.

Reports at the same gate and date can still be distinct events. Preserve event IDs when describing observations or failures; names and dates alone may not identify a unique record.
